column2: O, O you cupbearer, pass round a cup and hand it on / for love seemed easy at first, but difficulties fell
In hope of the musk-pod that the east wind at last opens from that lock of hair / from the twist of its musky curl, what blood fell into hearts
What safety of pleasure for me in the beloved's lodging, when every moment / the bell cries out: bind up the litters
Stain the prayer-rug with wine if the elder of the Magi tells you / for the wayfarer is not unaware of the way and custom of the stages
A dark night, and fear of the wave, and a whirlpool so terrible / how would the lightly laden of the shores know our state?
All my affairs, from self-will, drew me at last to ill fame / how can that secret stay hidden of which they make gatherings?
If you want presence, do not be absent from him, Hafez / when you meet the one you love, leave the world and let it go
Where is right conduct, and where am I, the ruined? / see the distance of the road, from where to where
My heart grew weary of the cloister and the cloak of hypocrisy / where is the monastery of the Magi, and where the pure wine?
What relation do right conduct and piety have to roguery? / where is hearing a sermon, where the song of the rebab?
What do the hearts of enemies grasp of the friend's face? / where a dead lamp? where the candle of the sun?
Since the dust of your threshold is the collyrium of our sight / where shall we go from this court, tell us, where?
Do not look at the apple of the chin, for there is a pit in the way / where are you going, O heart, in such haste, where?
It is gone! may its memory be sweet, the time of union / where did that coquetry go, and that reproach, where?
Do not hope for rest and sleep from Hafez, O friend / what is rest, which is patience, and sleep, where?
If that Turk of Shiraz takes our heart in hand / for his Hindu mole I would give Samarkand and Bukhara
Give, cupbearer, the remaining wine, for in paradise you will not find / the bank of the water of Roknabad and the rose-walk of Mosalla
Alas! these saucy, sweet-working, city-upsetting gypsies / so carried patience from the heart as Turks the tray of plunder
Of our unfinished love the beauty of the beloved has no need / of water and colour and mole and down, what need has a lovely face?
From that ever-increasing beauty Yusuf had, I knew / that love brings Zuleikha out from the veil of chastity
If you bestow abuse, or if a curse, I speak a blessing / a bitter answer becomes the ruby, sugar-chewing lip
Listen to advice, dear soul, for dearer than the soul they hold / fortunate young men, the counsel of the wise old man
Speak of the minstrel and wine, and seek less the secret of time / for no one solved and none will solve by wisdom this riddle
You spoke a ghazal and pierced pearls, come and sing it sweetly, Hafez / for over your verse the sky scatters the necklace of the Pleiades
East wind, kindly tell that graceful gazelle / that you have given us to mountain and desert
The sugar-seller, may his life be long, why / does he not inquire after the sugar-chewing parrot?
Did the pride of your beauty not give you leave, O rose / to ask after the lovesick nightingale?
With good nature and kindness one can hunt the people of vision / with bond and snare they do not catch the wise bird
I do not know for what reason there is no colour of friendship / in the straight-statured, dark-eyed, moon-faced ones
When you sit with the beloved and measure out wine / remember the lovers who measure out wind
No more than this can be said as a fault in your beauty / that the way of kindness and faith is not in the lovely face
In heaven no wonder if, at the words of Hafez / Venus's song brings the Messiah to dance
The heart goes from my hand, you men of heart, for God's sake / alas, the hidden secret will become manifest
We are shipwrecked; O favourable wind, rise up / it may be that I see again the face of the familiar one
The ten-day kindness of the turning sky is a fable and a spell / count it an opportunity, friend, to do good to friends
In the circle of rose and wine last night the nightingale sang sweetly / bring the morning wine, wake up, O you drunkards
O possessor of nobility, in thanks for your safety / one day inquire after the destitute dervish
The ease of the two worlds is the meaning of these two words / with friends, generosity; with enemies, forbearance
In the street of good name they gave us no passage / if you do not approve, change fate
That bitter one that the Sufi called the mother of vices / is more desirable and sweeter to us than the kiss of maidens
In the time of poverty strive in pleasure and drunkenness / for this alchemy of being makes a beggar a Qarun
Do not be rebellious, or like a candle from jealousy of you will burn / the heart-taker in whose hand hard granite is wax
The mirror of Alexander is the cup of wine; look / so that it may show you the state of the realm of Darius
The fair Persian-speakers are bestowers of life / cupbearer, give the good news to the pious rogues
Hafez did not put on by himself this wine-stained cloak / O pure-skirted sheikh, hold us excused
To the attendants of the sultan, who will carry this prayer? / that in thanks for kingship, do not drive the beggar from sight
From the demon-natured rival I take refuge in my God / perhaps that piercing meteor will give help, for God's sake!
If your black eyelash made a sign at our blood / think of its deceit and make no mistake, O beauty
You burn the heart of a world when you light up your cheek / what profit have you from this, that you show no forbearance?
All night I am in this hope, that the morning breeze / with a message from friends will caress the friend
What resurrection is it, dear soul, that you showed the lovers? / heart and soul a ransom for your face, show us your cheek
By God, give a draught to Hafez who rises at dawn / for the morning prayer will have an effect on you
Sufi, come, for the mirror of the cup is clear / so that you may see the purity of the ruby-coloured wine
Ask the secret inside the veil from the drunken rogues / for this state is not for the high-ranking ascetic
The Anqa becomes no one's prey; take up the snare / for there the snare always holds only wind in its hand
At the feast of time, drink one or two cups and go / that is, do not hope for lasting union
O heart, youth went and you picked no flower of pleasure / in old age do some art of honour and name
Strive in present pleasure, for when the watering-place was gone / Adam let go of paradise, the garden of the house of peace
We have on your threshold much right of service / O master, look again with pity on the servant
Hafez is a disciple of the cup of wine; O east wind, go / and from this servant carry service to the Sheikh of Jam
Cupbearer, rise and pass round the cup / throw dust on the head of the grief of days
Put the goblet of wine in my palm, so that from my breast / I may pull off this azure-coloured patched cloak
Though it is ill fame in the eyes of the wise / we do not want shame or name
Pass the wine; how long this wind of pride? / dust on the head of the self that comes to no good end
The smoke of the sigh of my lamenting breast / burned these frozen raw ones
A confidant of the secret of my own mad heart / I see no one, of the elect or the common
With a heart-easer my mind is glad / who carried rest from my heart all at once
He looks no more at the cypress in the meadow / whoever saw that silver-bodied cypress
Be patient, Hafez, in hardship, day and night / in the end one day you will find your desire
The splendour of the time of youth comes again to the garden / the good news of the rose reaches the sweet-voiced nightingale
O east wind, if you reach again the young ones of the meadow / carry our service to the cypress and the rose and the basil
If the young wine-selling Magian shows himself like this / I will make my eyelashes the sweepers of the tavern's door
O you who draw a polo-stick of pure ambergris over the moon / do not make me, the bewildered one, distraught
I fear this crowd who laugh at the dreg-drinkers / will lose their faith over the business of the tavern
Be a friend of the men of God, for in Noah's ark / there is a dust that would not buy the flood for a drop of water
Go out of the house of the sky and do not seek bread / for that black-bowled one kills the guest in the end
Whoever's sleeping-place at last is a handful of dust / say, what need to raise your hall to the heavens?
My moon of Canaan! the throne of Egypt has become yours / it is time that you bid farewell to the prison
Hafez, drink wine and be a rogue and be glad, but / do not, like others, make the Quran a snare of deceit
Last night from the mosque to the tavern came our elder / what, friends of the path, is our plan after this?
How shall we disciples turn our face toward the qibla, how? / our elder has his face toward the house of the wine-seller
In the tavern of the path we will lodge together / for so was our destiny decreed in the covenant of pre-eternity
If reason knew how glad the heart is in the bond of his hair / the wise would go mad in pursuit of our chain
Your fair face revealed to us a verse of grace / since that time there is nothing but grace and beauty in our commentary
With your stony heart, will it ever take hold one night / our fiery sigh and the burning of our night-waking breast?
The arrow of our sigh passes through the sky; Hafez, be silent / have mercy on your own soul, beware of our arrow
Cupbearer, light up our cup with the light of wine / minstrel, say that the world's affairs have gone as we wish
We have seen in the cup the reflection of the beloved's face / O you who are unaware of the pleasure of our constant drinking
He never dies whose heart was made alive by love / our permanence is recorded on the register of the world
The coquetry and airs of the straight-statured last only so long / until our pine-strutting cypress comes in its display
O wind, if you pass by the rose-garden of the loved ones / take care, present our message to the beloved
Say: why do you deliberately take our name out of memory? / the time will come itself when you do not remember our name
Drunkenness is sweet in the eye of our captivating beauty / for that reason they have given our rein to drunkenness
I fear that on the day of reckoning it will gain no advantage / the sheikh's lawful bread over our unlawful water
Hafez, keep scattering from your eye a grain of tears / it may be that the bird of union makes for our snare
The green sea of the sky and the ship of the new moon / are drowned in the bounty of our Haji Qavam
O you whose radiant face gives light to the moon of beauty / the lustre of loveliness is from the well of your chin
The soul that has come to the lips intends to see you / shall it go back or come out? what is your command?
No one in the era of your narcissus gained anything of well-being / better that they do not sell chastity to your drunken ones
Perhaps our sleep-heavy fortune will wake up / because your radiant face has splashed water on its eyes
Send with the east wind a bouquet of roses from your face / in hope that we smell a scent from the soil of your garden
May you have life and your desire, O cupbearers of Jamshid's feast / though our cup was not filled with wine in your era
The heart is going to ruin; let the heart-holder know / beware, O friends, by my soul and by your soul
O Lord, when will this aim be granted, that they become partners? / our collected mind and your dishevelled hair
Keep your skirt far from dust and blood when you pass by us / for on this road the slain are many, your sacrifices
Hafez is making a prayer; listen, say an amen / may our daily portion be your sugar-scattering ruby lip
O east wind, tell the dwellers of the city of Yazd from us / may the heads of the ungrateful be the ball for your polo-sticks
Though we are far from the carpet of nearness, our resolve is not far / we are servants of your king and singers of your praise
O king of kings of lofty star, for God's sake, a favour / so that like a star I may kiss the dust of your hall
The dawn is breaking and the cloud has hung its canopy / the morning wine, the morning wine, O companions
Dew is dripping on the face of the tulip / the wine, the wine, O loved ones
From the meadow blows the breeze of paradise / ho, drink pure wine breath after breath
The rose has set up an emerald throne in the meadow / seize the wine that is like fiery ruby
They have shut the door of the tavern again / open, O Opener of doors
Your lip and teeth have the rights of salt / over souls and breasts that are roasted
In such a season it would be strange / that they shut the tavern in haste
To the face of the fairy-bodied cupbearer / drink pure wine like Hafez
I said: O sultan of the fair, have mercy on this stranger / he said: following the heart, the poor stranger loses the way
I said to him: stay a while; he said: hold me excused / how can a home-bred one bear the grief of so many strangers?
What grief has a darling asleep on royal squirrel-fur / if the stranger makes his bed and pillow of thorn and granite?
O you in the chain of whose hair is the place of so many friends / strangely fitting fell that musky mole on the coloured cheek
The reflection of wine shows in the colour of your moon-like face / like a Judas-tree leaf on the page of a wild rose, strange
Very strange has fallen that ant-line of down around your face / though in a picture gallery a musky line is not strange
I said: O evening of strangers, your night-coloured lock / beware at dawn when this stranger laments
He said: Hafez, the familiar ones are in the station of bewilderment / it is no wonder if the stranger sits weary and wretched
O holy beauty, who will draw the cord of your veil? / and O bird of paradise, who gives you grain and water?
Sleep went from my eyes in this liver-burning thought / whose embrace has become the lodging of your rest and sleep?
You do not ask after the dervish, and I fear there is not / in you a thought of forgiveness or care for reward
That languorous eye waylaid the hearts of lovers / it is plain from this manner that your wine is strong
The arrow you shot at my heart from a glance went astray / let us see what your right judgment will think next
Every lament and cry I made, you did not hear / it is plain, O beauty, that your court is high
The source of water is far from this desert; be aware / lest the ghoul of the desert deceive you with a mirage
On the road of old age, by what custom will you go, O heart? / at any rate the days of your youth were spent in error
O heart-lighting palace that is the lodging of intimacy / O Lord, may the calamity of days not ruin you
Hafez is not a slave who flees from his master / make peace and come back, for I am ruined by your reproach
The curve that your saucy eyebrow set into its bow / it shot at the life of me, wretched and weak
The image of the two worlds was not yet, when there was the colour of affection / time did not lay the design of love only at this time
With one glance of coquetry when the narcissus showed itself off / the deceit of your eye threw a hundred troubles into the world
Having drunk wine and sweated, you go into the meadow / so that the lustre of your face set fire to the Judas-tree
To the feasting-place of the meadow last night I passed, drunk / when the bud put me in doubt about your mouth
The violet was knotting its twisted lock / the east wind threw into the midst the tale of your hair
From shame that I compared it to your face / the jasmine, by the east wind's hand, threw dust in its mouth
Out of piety I had not seen wine and minstrel before this / desire for the young Magians threw me into this and that
Now I wash the cloak with the water of ruby wine / the portion of pre-eternity cannot be thrown off oneself
Perhaps the opening for Hafez lay in this ruin / that the gift of pre-eternity threw him into the wine of the Magi
The world will now go as I wish, for the turning of time / threw me into the service of the master of the world
The breast burned from the fire of the heart in grief for the beloved / there was a fire in this house so that the dwelling burned
My body melted by reason of the distance of the heart-taker / my soul burned from the fire of love for the beloved's face
See the burning of the heart: from so much fire of my tears, the candle's heart / last night burned for me out of love, like a moth
It is no wonder that a friend is the one who burns for me / when I went out of myself, the heart of the stranger burned
The water of the tavern carried away my cloak of piety / the fire of the wine-house burned the house of my reason
Like a cup my heart broke from the repentance I made / like a tulip my liver burned without wine and the wine-house
Make less of the quarrel and come back, for the pupil of my eye / took the cloak off its head and burned it in thanksgiving
Leave off the tale, Hafez, and drink wine a while / for we did not sleep tonight, and the candle burned over the tale
Cupbearer, may the coming of the feast be blessed for you / and those promises you made, may they not go from your memory
I am amazed that in this length of the days of separation / you took your heart from your companions, and your heart allowed you
Carry service to the daughter of the vine; say, come out / for our breath and resolve have set you free from bondage
The joy of the company is in your step and your arrival / may that heart be the place of grief that does not wish you glad
Thanks be to God that from the plunder of autumn no breach was found / in your garden of jasmine and cypress and rose and boxwood
Far be the evil eye, for from that dispersion it brought you back / your renowned star and the fortune you were born with
Hafez, do not let go the fortune of this ark of Noah / or else the flood of events will carry away your foundation
O breeze of dawn, where is the beloved's resting-place? / where is the lodging of that lover-killing, artful moon?
The night is dark, and the road of the valley of Ayman ahead / where is the fire of Sinai, where the appointed time of meeting?
Whoever came into the world bears the mark of ruin / in the tavern ask: where is the sober one?
He is the one fit for good tidings who understands a hint / there are many subtle points; where is the confidant of secrets?
Every tip of my hair has a thousand affairs with you / where are we, and where is the idle blamer?
Ask again of his tresses, fold upon fold / where is this grief-stricken, bewildered, captive heart?
Reason went mad; where is that musky chain? / the heart withdrew from us; where is the heart-holder's eyebrow?
Cupbearer and minstrel and wine are all ready, but / pleasure without the beloved is not ready; where is the beloved?
Hafez, do not be grieved by the autumn wind in the meadow of time / think a reasonable thought: where is the rose without a thorn?
The fast went aside and the feast came and hearts rose up / wine came to a boil in the wine-house, and one must ask for wine
The turn of the heavy-souled sellers of piety has passed / the time of roguery and of the rogues' rejoicing is plain
What blame is there for one who drinks such wine? / what fault is this, in such folly? and what error is this?
A wine-drinker in whom there is no pretence and hypocrisy / is better than a piety-seller in whom there is pretence and hypocrisy
We are not hypocritical rogues and companions of duplicity / He who is the knower of secrets is witness to this state
We perform God's duty and do no harm to anyone / and what they say is not permitted, we do not say is permitted
What happens if you and I drink a few cups of wine? / wine is from the blood of vines, not from your blood
My heart and faith are gone, and the heart-taker rose in reproach / he said: do not sit with us, for safety has gone from you
Who have you heard of who sat happily a moment at this feast / who did not rise in regret at the end of the company?
If the candle made a boast with its tongue of that laughing lip / it stood nights before your lovers in penalty
In the meadow the spring wind, from beside the rose and the cypress / rose up in devotion to that cheek and stature
You passed by drunk, and from the secluded ones of the heavenly kingdom / at the sight of you the tumult of resurrection rose
Before your gait, from shame, it did not lift its foot / the unruly cypress that had risen in pride of height and stature
Hafez, throw off this cloak; perhaps you will save your life / for fire has risen from the cloak of hypocrisy and wonder-working
When you hear the words of the people of heart, do not say it is wrong / you are no knower of words, my soul; the error is here
My head does not bow to this world and the next / blessed be God, these troubles that are in our head
Inside me, heart-weary, I do not know who it is / for I am silent, and he is in lament and in uproar
My heart went out of tune; where are you, O minstrel? / play a lament, ho, for in this mode our affairs are in harmony
I never had any regard for the affairs of the world / your face adorned it so sweetly in my sight
I have not slept, from a fancy my heart is cooking / I have a hangover of a hundred nights; where is the wine-house?
Since the cloister has been stained with my heart's blood / if you wash me with wine, the right is on your side
For this they hold me dear in the monastery of the Magi / that a fire that does not die is always in our heart
What tune was it that the minstrel was playing in the mode / that life went, and still my brain is full of longing
The call of your love was sounded inside last night / the space of Hafez's breast is still full of the echo
The image of your face is our companion on every road / the breeze of your hair is the bond of our aware soul
In spite of the claimants who forbid love / the beauty of your face is our well-founded proof
See what the apple of your chin is saying / a thousand Egyptian Yusufs have fallen into our well
If our hand does not reach your long hair / it is the fault of our dishevelled fortune and our short hand
Tell the chamberlain at the door of the private retreat / so-and-so is one of those who sit in the corner on the dust of our threshold
Though in form he is veiled from our sight / he is always in the sight of our untroubled mind
If Hafez knocks at a door once in a year, open / for it is years that he has longed for the moon-like face
Do not seek obedience and covenant and right conduct from me, drunk / for I became famous for drinking cups on the day of Alast
The very moment I made ablution from the spring of love / I spoke the four takbirs once and for all over everything that is
Give wine, so that I may inform you of the secret of fate / by whose face I became a lover, and by whose scent drunk
The mountain's waist here is less than the ant's waist / do not despair of the door of mercy, O wine-worshipper
Except that drunken narcissus, may the evil eye not reach it / under this turquoise vault no one sat happily
May my soul be a ransom for his mouth, for in the garden of vision / the world's meadow-adorner formed no sweeter bud than this
Hafez, by the fortune of your love, became a Solomon / that is, of union with you he has nothing in hand but wind
The red rose has bloomed and the nightingale has become drunk / the call to merriment, O wine-worshipping Sufis
The foundation of repentance that seemed as firm as stone / see how wondrously a glass cup has broken it
Bring wine, for in the court of self-sufficiency / what is watchman and what is sultan, what is sober and what drunk
From this inn of two doors, since departure is necessary / the portico and arch of living, what matter whether high or low
The station of pleasure is not attained without pain / yes, by the decree of affliction they bound the covenant of Alast
Do not trouble your mind over being and not-being, and be glad / for not-being is the end of every perfection there is
Asaf's majesty and the wind-horse and the speech of birds / went to the wind, and the master gained nothing from it
Do not leave the road on wing and feather, for the shot arrow / took to the air a while, but sat down in the dust
Hafez, how can the tongue of your pen give thanks for this / that they carry the speech of your words from hand to hand
Hair dishevelled and sweating and lips laughing and drunk / shirt torn and singing a ghazal and a flask in hand
His narcissus seeking a brawl and his lip mocking / at midnight last night he came to my pillow and sat down
He brought his head to my ear and in a sad voice / said: O my old lover, are you asleep?
A lover who is given such night-time wine / is an infidel to love if he does not become a wine-worshipper
Go, O ascetic, and find no fault with the dreg-drinkers / for they gave us no gift but this on the day of Alast
What he poured into our cup we drank / whether it is the wine of paradise or the wine of drunkenness
The laughter of the cup of wine and the knot-tying hair of the beauty / O how many a repentance, like Hafez's repentance, have they broken
Into the monastery of the Magi came my beloved, a cup in hand / drunk with wine, and the wine-drinkers drunk with his drunken narcissus
In the shoe of his steed the shape of the new moon is seen / and beside his tall stature the height of the pine is low
After all, how can I say I am aware of myself, when I am not / and why should I say my gaze is not with him, when it is
The candle of my intimate heart sat down when he rose / and the lament of the gazers rose when he sat down
If the musk-perfume became fragrant, it twined in his tresses / and if the woad became a bow-drawer, it joined in his eyebrow
Come back, so that Hafez's lost life may come back / although the arrow that has left the thumb-ring does not come back
By the master's soul and the ancient right and the true covenant / the companion of my morning breath is the prayer for your fortune
My tears, which outdo the flood of Noah / could not wash the image of your love from the tablet of the breast
Make a deal, and buy this broken heart / for with its brokenness it is worth a hundred thousand whole ones
The ant's tongue grew long against Asaf, and rightly / for the master lost the seal of Jamshid and did not seek it again
O heart, do not cut off hope from the friend's endless kindness / since you boasted of love, stake your head, quick and nimble
Strive for truth, so that the sun may be born from your breath / for from lying the first dawn became black-faced
Through you I became mad for mountain and plain, and still / you do not out of pity loosen the belt of the chain
Do not be grieved, Hafez, and do not seek constancy from heart-takers / what is the garden's fault when this plant did not grow?
Through the image of you, what care have we for wine? / tell the jar to go its way, for the wine-house is in ruin
If it is the wine of paradise, pour it out, for without the friend / every sweet drink you give me is torment itself
Alas, the heart-taker is gone, and in the weeping eye / the drawing of the image of his down is a picture on water
Wake up, O eye, for one cannot be safe / from this constant flood that is in this lodging of sleep
The beloved passes openly by you, but / strangers are looking, so the veil is drawn
When the rose saw the grace of sweat on your coloured cheek / in the fire of longing, from the grief of the heart, it is drowned in rosewater
Valley and plain are green; come, let us not let go / of the water's edge, for the whole world is a mirage
Do not seek a place for advice in the corner of my brain / for this corner is full of the murmur of harp and rebab
Hafez, what of it if he is a lover and a rogue and a gazer / many strange ways are proper to the days of youth
Your hair bound a thousand hearts with a single strand / it closed the road of a thousand remedy-seekers from four sides
So that lovers may give their life at the scent of its breeze / it opened a musk-pod and closed the door of desire
I went mad because my beauty, like the new moon / showed an eyebrow and made a display and covered the face
The cupbearer poured wine of several colours into the cup / see these patterns, how sweetly he set them in the gourd
O Lord, what glance did the flask make, that the jar's blood / with the cries of its gurgle stuck in its throat
What mode did the minstrel make, that in the mode of sama / he closed the door of shouting on the people of ecstasy and state
Hafez, whoever did not practise love and wanted union / put on the pilgrim's garb to circle the Kaaba of the heart without ablution
That Night of Power which the people of retreat speak of is tonight / O Lord, in which star is this influence of fortune?
So that the hands of the unworthy may seldom reach your tresses / every heart from a ring is in the remembrance of O Lord, O Lord
I am slain by the well of your chin, for from every side / a hundred thousand necks of souls are under the collar of its dimple
My royal rider, for whose face the moon holds the mirror / the crown of the high sun is the dust of his mount's shoe
See the sweat's reflection on his cheek, for the hot-faced sun / in longing for that sweat has fever every day as long as it is
I will not give up the beloved's ruby and the cup of wine / ascetics, hold me excused, for this is my creed
At that hour when they saddle the back of the east wind / how shall I ride with Solomon, I whose mount is an ant?
He who shoots a dart at my heart from the corner of an eye / the food of Hafez's soul is in his smile under the lip
The water of life drips from the beak of its eloquence / my pen's crow, in God's name, how lofty its drinking-place
When God shaped the form of your heart-opening eyebrow / He tied the opening of my affairs to your coquetries
It sat me and the meadow's cypress in the dust of the road / when time fastened the linen of your narcissus robe
It undid a hundred knots from our affairs and the bud's heart / when the rose's breeze set its heart on longing for you
The turning of the wheel made me content with your bond / but what use, since it tied the thread's end to your consent
Do not tie a knot like a musk-pod on my wretched heart / for it made a covenant with the tip of your knot-loosening hair
You yourself were another union, O breeze of union / see the error, that the heart set its hope on your faithfulness
From the hand of your cruelty I said, I will leave the city / laughing he said: Hafez, go; who has tied your foot?
What need has one who chose retreat for sightseeing? / since there is the friend's street, what need for the open plain?
Dear soul, by the need you have with God / at last ask for a moment what need we have
O king of beauty, for God's sake, we have burned / at last ask what need the beggar has
We are people of need and have no tongue to ask / in the presence of the generous, what need for wishing?
There is no need for a story if your aim is our blood / since the goods are yours, what need for plunder?
The friend's luminous mind is a world-showing cup / to declare one's need, what need is there?
That time is gone when I bore the boatman's favour / when the pearl has come to hand, what need for the sea?
O claimant, go, for I have no business with you / the loved ones are present, what need for enemies?
O beggar lover, since the beloved's spirit-giving lip / knows your allowance, what need for demanding?
Hafez, you end it, for art becomes plain by itself / what need for quarrel and dispute with the claimant?
